source: Curated from W. A. Wright, The Bible Word-Book (2nd ed., 1884; public domain), with modern definitions
_rules: trigger is a case-sensitive regex; a rule shows its note once when the trigger matches anywhere on the page

rules.title: -eth endings
rules.meaning: An old verb ending for he, she or it: goeth = goes, saith = says, hath = has, doth = does.

rules.title: -est and -st endings
rules.meaning: An old verb ending used with thou: thou knowest = you know, thou art = you are, thou hast = you have, thou didst = you did.

rules.title: thou, thee, ye
rules.meaning: Thou, thee, thy and thine address one person; ye and you address more than one. The KJV keeps this difference, which modern English has lost: in Luke 22:31-32 Satan desired to have "you" (all the disciples), but Jesus prayed for "thee" (Peter).

entries.note: Never "talk". In Philippians 3:20 it means citizenship.

entries.meaning: to go before, come to meet
entries.note: From Latin praevenire, to come before; not "to stop".
Elsewhere let has its modern sense, as in "let us".
The self-giving love of 1 Corinthians 13, not giving to the poor.
"The quick and the dead" means the living and the dead.

entries.meaning: to make alive, give life to

entries.note: A "meat offering" is a grain offering, with no meat in it.

entries.meaning: grain, such as wheat or barley
entries.note: Not maize, which was unknown in the ancient Near East.
"Suffer the little children to come unto me" means let them come. In other places it means to undergo pain.
"Be careful for nothing" (Philippians 4:6) means do not be anxious about anything.
Much stronger than the modern sense of a misbehaving child.

entries.meaning: to share, especially with those in need
a place or seat, especially at a meal
entries.note: "The uppermost rooms" are the best seats at a feast.
"The Holy Ghost" is the Holy Spirit; "gave up the ghost" means died.

entries.meaning: often: the heart, deep feelings, compassion
the kidneys; the innermost self, thoughts and feelings
to prove by setting out evidence

entries.note: Sometimes "to know", as in 2 Corinthians 8:1, "we do you to wit" (we make known to you).
"An help meet for him" means a helper suitable for him.
The opposite of its modern sense of "eventually".

entries.meaning: a denarius, a labourer's daily wage
entries.note: Greek denarion; much more valuable than a modern penny.
As a question it means why; at the start of a statement it means therefore.
